No. mtime is wrong here. On CI every file looks freshly checked out so nothing is ever cached. Key on a hash of the source file bytes plus the importer version.

turns.assistant: AVX2 is not faster. perf shows the encode loop is memory bound on the 64 MB source image, cache misses dominate. Compute is not the limit.

turns.user: OK, shelve SIMD. If bake time matters we look at tiling the source reads.
Should we share the bake cache across the team through an S3 bucket?

tool.output:
src/bake.rs:140:    let weight = (luma as f32).powf(2.2);
src/bake.rs:141:    key.update(&weight.to_bits().to_le_bytes());

turns.assistant: Baked output depends on float math (powf, fused multiply-add on some CPUs), so the same source can bake to different bytes on different machines. A shared cache would flip artifacts between builds and break reproducible comparisons.

turns.user: Then no shared cache. Keep it per machine in .bakecache.
